target: Passengers booked on Kestrel flights departing or arriving in Orlando or Philadelphia between December 21 and January 3

actions.action: Backup ground handling at both bases for strike days
Free changes and cancellations in a 2-week window
Partner airline rebooking for 2 disrupted weeks

message: Kestrel Air update: workers at our ground handling contractor plan a 48-hour strike at Orlando and Philadelphia on Dec 22-23. We have hired backup ground crews at both airports, but some flights may still be delayed or canceled. If you are booked Dec 21-Jan 3, you can change or cancel your flight for free in the app. If your flight is canceled, we will rebook you on Kestrel or a partner airline, or refund you. We will text you as soon as anything changes.
why: The strike hits the busiest week of the year and week 8 is 97% booked, so there are no spare Kestrel seats.
Backup crews keep flights running; free changes move flexible travelers off Dec 22-23 before it starts.
Partner rebooking is the only way to rebook 90% of affected passengers within 24 hours.

target: Passengers whose Kestrel flight is canceled or delayed more than 3 hours from December 21

actions.action: Hotel rooms held for stranded passengers, whatever the cause
Extra airport and call-center staff for 2 weeks
Goodwill for up to 10,000 affected passengers

message: Kestrel Air: we are sorry your trip was disrupted. If you are stranded overnight, for any reason, we have a hotel room held for you - show this message at the Kestrel desk. Extra staff are at the Orlando and Philadelphia airports and on our phone lines. You will also receive a $75 Kestrel travel credit. You can rebook or request a refund in the app; your refund rights under DOT rules are unchanged.
why: Passengers remember how they were treated more than the delay itself.
Hotels for any cause and extra staff cut wait times and complaints on the worst days.
A $75 credit is cheap because most are used on empty seats, and it brings travelers back.
